title: Worker records upsert; payload keys pinned; cells update arms the behavior door
action: Review B-P2-6 + B-P2-8. (1) push_worker_record upserts by (nickname, cell): an existing record with the same pair is updated in place (tier/status refreshed), never duplicated — run_worker_add and register_worker_for_cell both inherit it; a same-nickname different-cell pair still appends (legitimate multi-cell worker). Test: double add of the same pair yields one record; update then hits the live one. (2) Payload pins: tests through run_dispatch_prepare (the real entry, not the inner fn) asserting worker_registered:true on a successful claim and registration_error naming the failure when registration fails. (3) cells update: when an update sets change_class to behavior and the same call does not explicitly set behavior_change, arm trace.behavior_change=true (explicit false in the same call wins; setting change_class AWAY from behavior changes nothing). Reuse the same defaulting logic as validate.rs's normalize_new_cell — one shared function, not a copy. TDD red-first: update-to-behavior arms the door (assert via resolve_declared_behavior_change); explicit-false honored; away-from-behavior untouched. NOTE: the instruction-layer sync (swarming reference teaching manual worker add) is deliberately NOT in this cell — the orchestrator owes it as a docs-lane edit with the regen chain at capture time.

truths: double registration of the same nickname+cell yields one record and update mutates the live one
worker_registered/registration_error asserted through the real dispatch prepare entry
cells update to change_class behavior arms the scribing door under the same rules as add

artifacts.substantive: upsert plus tests; shared defaulting used by update path
